course_name_original: Calcul de structures Eléments Finis avancé
prerequisites: introductory finite element module in M11
basic structural design course in M12

learning_outcomes.text: Model structures such as plates numerically, using assumptions adapted to each context.
Discretize a domain using an appropriate mesh.
Establish elementary matrices (stiffness, mass) and solve the associated matrix systems.
Critically interpret results obtained, taking into account the assumptions and limitations inherent in the models used.
Possess theoretical knowledge, practical numerical modeling skills and a critical eye for results, enabling them to apply these tools effectively in industrial or academic contexts.

Grasp the fundamental principles of FEM, such as variational formulation, discretization and assembly of elementary matrices, and the theoretical foundations of mechanical and numerical modeling of plate-based structures.
Integrate the notions of convergence, mesh accuracy and interpretation of results.
Carry out a complete modeling of a mechanical problem.
Choose the appropriate mechanical model (1D, 2D or 3D).
Generate a structured or free mesh and apply boundary conditions and loads.
Be familiar with the use of Abaqus software for numerical simulation of structures.
Develop methodological rigor essential to the implementation of numerical simulations.
Be aware of the limits of the models used and adopt a critical attitude towards the results obtained.

syllabus_topics: Linear elastic behavior laws and extension to composites
Study of plate-based structures in diaphragm and bending modes
Practical work on Abaqus FE code for structural design

assessment_methods.method: DS1 (presumably a written exam or project)

assessment_rules: The evaluation formula is (1.2 * DS1 + 0.8 * TP1) / 2. This implies DS1 has a 60% weight and TP1 has a 40% weight.
bibliography: J. C. Craveur. Modélisation des Structures; Calcul par Eléments Finis. Masson, 1997.
J. L. Batoz. Modélisation des structues par éléments finis - Poutres et plaques. Hermes, 1990.
J. Fish, T. Belytschko. A first course in finite elements. Wiley, 2007.
degree: Titre d'ingénieur ENIT (cycle ingénieur, semestres 5-10; orientación mecánica/producción)
